role.altitude: Her week is still the complaint on the floor, the instruction beside the equipment, the choice of what to buy, and the figures she will stand behind. She stops hunting a stored complaint, a stored procedure, and a column that is already on a row.
skills_to_grow: Leave a blank function line or a blank expense unread rather than guess it
Show the equipment herself even when the procedure is on the screen
Match the item in front of her to the line she is about to order
Keep a named cleaner's hours out of any ranking
role.ambitious_version: She still investigates on site, still instructs in the room, and still chooses what to buy. A report line with no stored figure stays blank until she writes it, and no list speaks for her.

tasks.short: Investigate a complaint and take the corrective action.

steps.what: List open complaints about this service or equipment.
Investigate that service and that equipment on site.
Decide the corrective action for the complaint.
Tell the cleaner the corrective action to take.
Write the corrective action taken against the complaint.

tasks.design: The complaint record in {HELPDESK} lists the room, the service or equipment, and the reported problem only when those fields are already stored. She investigates on site, decides the corrective action, tells the cleaner, and writes the action herself. The list does not decide the action, does not fill a sheet, and does not send an alert.
tasks.previous_blocker: The complaint was a phone note or a remark at the desk, and the room still had to be seen before anyone knew what to fix.
tasks.enabler_now: A ticket can show a room and a reported problem that someone already logged. Seeing the equipment and choosing the fix are still a visit.
tasks.still_hard: A complaint about a smell, a missed room, or a machine that only fails sometimes is not settled by the text on the ticket.
tasks.human_edge: She can see whether the service failed or the equipment failed, and she is the one who tells the cleaner what to change.
tasks.altitude: She still investigates and still chooses the corrective action. She stops searching for a complaint that is already on a ticket. She does not gain a right to close it without the visit.

reach.task: Redo the service the complaint names in that room.
reach.learn: Which room and which failure the ticket already states, so a blank ticket is not treated as a known fault.

evidence.claim: Where the Dutch works-council rule applies, tying inspection or complaint results to a named cleaner can be a check on performance, and staff data of that kind needs consent. This record states the corrective action. It does not score the cleaner.
An automated decision with a significant effect needs a person who can intervene. The corrective action is her decision after the visit. The list does not take it.
The range is a scenario for a complaint she still has to see. It is not a published time study. Model knowledge.

assumptions: Complaint fields are complaint id, room or area, service or equipment name, and the reported problem. The producer is whoever logged it before this task, at the desk or from the client. That capture is outside this task and is not counted as time saved.
If room, service or equipment, or the reported problem is blank, the list step does not run and she hears the complaint in person. A blank is not filled with a guess.
Investigating, deciding the corrective action, telling the cleaner, and writing the action stay at full time. The only shortened step is hunting a complaint that is already logged.
The list does not assign the action, does not fill a sheet, and does not send an alert. The written action is not a score of the cleaner.
Upkeep is 0.2 hours per 100 baseline hours of this task, for telling the desk when the logged room is wrong. That telling is her own speech. The list does not send it.
unknowns: Whether complaints at this site are already a ticket with room and equipment, or still a verbal remark.
Whether this workplace is covered by the Dutch works-council rule.
research_questions: On a week of complaints, how often are room, service or equipment, and the problem filled before she leaves the desk?
How often is the logged room not the room where the fault is?

incremental.description: Tell the desk when the logged room is the wrong one. The list does not send that message.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: When complaint id, room, service or equipment, and the reported problem are already stored, she skips hunting the note. When any of those is blank, or the room is wrong, she hears it and looks as today, and the saving is near zero. The visit, the decision, telling the cleaner, and writing the action are not shortened.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Instruct staff in procedures and equipment maintenance.

steps.what: List the stored work policy for this equipment.
Instruct staff in the work policies and procedures.
Instruct staff in use and maintenance of the equipment.

tasks.design: The procedure store in {DOCS} lists the policy name and the stored procedure steps for this equipment only when those fields are already filled. She instructs staff in the work policies and procedures, and in the use and maintenance of the equipment. The list does not instruct, does not send the policy, and does not raise an alert.
tasks.previous_blocker: The procedure sat in a binder or in her head, and the new cleaner was already beside the machine.
tasks.enabler_now: A document store can show a policy name and the steps a maintainer already filed. Instructing still means she is in the room.
tasks.still_hard: A cleaner who has not used the machine needs the motion shown. A procedure written for a different machine is not something she should read out.
tasks.human_edge: She sees whether the cleaner's hands followed the step, and she stops the equipment if they did not.
tasks.altitude: She still instructs staff in the policies and on the equipment. She stops paging a binder when the procedure is stored. She does not gain a right to mark someone instructed because a card was opened.

reach.task: Maintain the equipment the procedure names.
reach.learn: Which maintenance step the stored procedure actually states, so a blank procedure is not treated as already taught.

evidence.claim: A customer chatbot must say it is AI. This design does not instruct staff through a chatbot, and it does not speak the procedure to them.
The range is a scenario for instruction given in the room. It is not a published time study. Model knowledge.

assumptions: Policy-card fields are equipment id, policy name, and the procedure steps as stored text. The producer is whoever approved the procedure into the store before this task. That capture is outside this task and is not counted as time saved.
If policy name or the procedure steps are blank, or they name different equipment, the list step does not run and she teaches from the binder or from memory. A blank step is not invented.
Both instruction steps stay at full time. The only shortened step is hunting the procedure when it is already stored.
The list does not instruct staff, does not send the policy, and does not raise an alert. Opening the card is not a record that someone was trained.
Upkeep is 0.2 hours per 100 baseline hours of this task, for telling the person who keeps the procedure when a stored step is out of date. That telling is her own speech. The list does not send it.
unknowns: Whether this site's procedures are stored as text against an equipment id, or only as a paper binder.
How often the stored procedure is for a different machine than the one in the room.
research_questions: On a week of instruction, how often is the policy name and the procedure text filled before she starts?
When it is filled, does she still fetch the binder?

incremental.description: Tell the person who keeps the procedure when a stored step is out of date. The list does not send that message.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: When equipment id, policy name, and the procedure steps are already stored for this machine, she skips hunting the binder. When they are blank or for another machine, she teaches as today and the saving is near zero. Instructing staff in the policies and in the use and maintenance of the equipment is not shortened.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Select and order equipment, supplies or furnishings.

steps.what: List on-hand quantity and reorder point for these supplies.
Select the equipment, supplies or furnishings in front of her.
Decide the quantity to order or purchase.
Draft order lines for the equipment, supplies or furnishings she selected.
Check the draft names only those selected supplies and furnishings.
Place that order or purchase with the supplier.

tasks.design: The supplies record in {OTHER} lists item, on-hand quantity, reorder point and unit price only when those fields are stored, and it drafts order lines only for the equipment, supplies or furnishings she selected and the quantity she named. She checks that the draft names those items and no others, then places the order or purchase herself. The draft does not send the order and does not raise an alert.
tasks.previous_blocker: On-hand quantity lived in a cupboard count or a private sheet, and the order was typed again into a mail to the supplier.
tasks.enabler_now: A supplies record can show a reorder point and a unit price that someone already keeps, and it can copy the lines she has already chosen. It cannot see the cupboard.
tasks.still_hard: Furnishings and machines still have to be looked at. A wrong unit price or a substitute the supplier offers is still her call, and she still places the order.
tasks.human_edge: She can tell a worn machine from one that only looks short on the list, and she is the person the supplier hears from.
tasks.altitude: She still selects what to buy and still places the order. She stops retyping lines when the item, the quantity she named, and the unit price are already stored. She does not gain a right to let a draft order itself.

reach.task: Use the supplies once they arrive on the floor.
reach.learn: Which item and quantity were on the order she placed, so a substitute is not put in use as if it were the one she selected.

evidence.claim: The range is a scenario for a housekeeping cupboard and a supplier mail. A reorder list is configuration of stored item, quantity and price. It is not a published time study. Model knowledge.

assumptions: Shortage fields are item id, item name, on-hand quantity, reorder point and unit price. The producer is whoever counts the cupboard and whoever maintains the price, before this task. That capture is outside this task and is not counted as time saved.
If on-hand quantity, reorder point or unit price is blank, the list or the draft does not invent it. She counts or she asks the price, and she writes that line when she places the order.

Selecting by looking, deciding the quantity, checking the draft, and placing the order or purchase stay at full time. The shortened steps are the shortage list and the draft of lines she has already chosen.
The draft does not send the order, does not post it to a ledger, and does not raise an alert. She places the order herself. The order is not a score of her spending.

Upkeep is 0.3 hours per 100 baseline hours of this task, for correcting a stored unit price before she places the order. Reading the draft for an item she did not select is already in the check and is not deducted again.
unknowns: Whether on-hand quantity and unit price are stored for the supplies she buys, or only a paper count.
Whether she orders by mail or buys at a counter for this site.
research_questions: On a month of orders, how often are item, on-hand quantity, reorder point and unit price filled before she selects?
How often does the supplier substitute an item after she has placed the order?

already_counted.description: Read the draft for an item or a furnishing she did not select.

incremental.description: Correct a stored unit price before she places the order. The draft does not send that correction.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: When item, on-hand quantity, reorder point and unit price are stored, and she has already named the quantity, she skips assembling those lines. When a price is blank, she is choosing furnishings in a showroom, or the draft names something she did not select, the saving is near zero. Looking, deciding the quantity, checking, and placing the order or purchase are not shortened.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Prepare the activity report from stored figures.

steps.what: List stored occupancy, hours worked, facility usage and departmental expenses.
Notice work performed that those rows do not show.
Ask staff about activity and personnel the rows omit.
Draft the activity reports from the stored rows.
Write each blank line on the activity report.
Check the report states only stored occupancy, hours and expenses.
File the checked activity report in the record.

tasks.design: The occupancy and hours record in {OTHER} and the expense lines in {ERP} are copied into a draft activity report only when those figures are already stored, and a missing figure stays blank. She writes each blank line and checks the report, and the file step then writes that checked version into {DOCS}. The draft does not file, nothing sends the report, and nothing raises an alert.
tasks.previous_blocker: Occupancy, hours, usage and expenses sat in separate sheets, and the monthly report was retyped before anyone could read it.
tasks.enabler_now: Those figures can be copied into a layout when they are already stored. A blank stays blank. Copying is not a judgement about the floor.
tasks.still_hard: Work performed that nobody logged, and a hour that does not match the floor, still have to be noticed and written by her before the report is filed.
tasks.human_edge: She knows whether the floor she walked matches the hours on the row, and she is accountable for the report she files.
tasks.altitude: She still notices the floor, still asks staff, and still writes every blank line. She stops retyping figures that are already stored. Filing happens only after she has checked that version, and she does not gain a right to send it on.

reach.task: Record the rooms cleaned on the shift.
reach.learn: Which room count is already a stored row, so a missing count stays blank on the activity report instead of being guessed.

evidence.claim: FacilityApps schedules per site and employee, takes clock-in, keeps digital work orders, and shows dashboards for clients. The vendor says 500 or more cleaning companies. That shows a cleaning suite can hold hours and a client view. The vendor count is not time saved on this report. This draft copies stored figures and does not invent one.

The FacilityApps quality app uses predefined inspection forms, photos as evidence, and reports for clients. A stored work-performed row may come from such a form. This report does not turn a photo into hours or into departmental expenses.

Where the Dutch works-council rule applies, hours and inspection results tied to named cleaners can check attendance or performance, and staff data of that kind needs consent. This report can show hours worked. It does not rank the cleaners.
A system that scores workers is the high-risk case in Annex III. This draft copies stored occupancy, hours, usage and expenses. It does not score personnel.
An automated decision with a significant effect needs a person who can intervene. Filing the report is not a decision on pay or discipline. She checks the version before the file step writes it.

A Dutch case fined a maintenance firm EUR 15,000 for recording sickness causes and leaving absence records open without authentication. This report does not record why someone was absent, and the filed report is not left open.
The range is a scenario for a monthly activity report. It is not a published time study. No measured case of time saved on this report was in the digest. Model knowledge.

assumptions: Figure fields are period, occupancy count, hours worked, facility usage, work-performed row, and departmental expense amount with cost centre. Occupancy and usage are produced by the front office, hours by the clock-in already in use, work performed by an inspection row if one exists, and expenses by finance. Those captures are outside this task and are not counted as time saved.
If a figure is blank, the draft leaves that line blank. She writes it from the floor or from what staff told her. The draft does not estimate a number.

Noticing the floor, asking staff, writing blank lines, and checking the report stay at full time. The shortened steps are listing stored figures, copying them into the draft, and filing the checked version.

The file step writes only the checked version activity-report-v1 into the document store. A later change voids that check. The draft does not file, nothing sends the report to a client, and nothing raises an alert.
The report is not a ranking of personnel and does not record why someone was absent. Where named hours can be used to monitor staff, works-council consent is part of access, not a saving.

Upkeep is 0.4 hours per 100 baseline hours of this task, for correcting a filed report when a stored hour was wrong. Reading the report for a figure the rows do not hold is already in the check and is not deducted again.
unknowns: Which of occupancy, hours, usage and expenses are already stored for this site before she starts the report.
Whether named cleaners' hours in this report are treated as a monitoring tool at this workplace.
research_questions: On a month of reports, how many of occupancy, hours worked, facility usage and departmental expenses are filled before she opens the sheet?
How often does a stored hour disagree with the floor she walked?

already_counted.description: Read the report for a figure the stored rows do not hold, including a blank she has just written.

incremental.description: Correct the filed report when a stored hour was wrong. The file step does not send that correction.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: When occupancy, hours worked, facility usage and departmental expenses are already stored, she skips retyping those lines and the checked version is filed without retyping. When she had to notice work performed, ask staff, or write a blank line, that time stays, and a month of empty rows saves nothing. Noticing, asking, writing blanks, and checking are not shortened. The figure is not the vendor's count of cleaning companies.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional
